task.title: The full project cycle
task.description:
Git is already set up, you are in your home folder. The ~/my-site folder contains your website (index.html, css/style.css, js/main.js), as well as the node_modules/ folder and the .env file with a secret key - but there is no repository. An empty repository https://github.com/anna/my-site.git has been created on "GitHub". Write the commands one per line: 1) Go to my-site and create a repository. 2) Create .gitignore with the lines node_modules/ and .env and check git status -s. 3) Make the first commit with all the website files: Add site files. 4) Create the feature/contacts branch, and in it - the file contacts.html with the text

Contacts

and the commit Add contacts page. 5) Go back to main, merge the branch (with --no-ff or fast-forward) and delete it. 6) Set up the global alias lg for log --oneline --graph --all and look at the history with git lg. 7) Connect the remote repository as origin and push main with upstream. 8) Create an annotated tag v1.0 with a message, push it to the server and check git status. As a result, the server has the main branch with your history and the tag v1.0 on the last commit, while node_modules and .env are not in any commit.
task.starter_code:
# Write the commands one per line. Lines starting with # are comments. # You are in your home folder. ~/my-site has a website, plus node_modules/ and .env, and no repository. # 1. Go to my-site and create a repository # 2. Create .gitignore with the lines node_modules/ and .env, check git status -s # 3. The first commit with all website files: Add site files # 4. The feature/contacts branch: the file contacts.html with the text

Contacts

, the commit Add contacts page # 5. Go back to main, merge the branch and delete it # 6. The lg alias for log --oneline --graph --all (global) and a call to git lg # 7. Connect origin, push main with upstream # 8. An annotated tag v1.0 and pushing it to the server, check git status

tests.name: The repository is created in ~/my-site, .gitignore with node_modules/ and .env exists
tests.check: (() => { const R = sim.repo("~/my-site"); const S = sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/my-site.git"); if (!R || R.root !== "/home/student/my-site") return false; const c = R.commit("main"); return Boolean(c && c.files[".gitignore"] !== undefined && R.isIgnored("node_modules/x.js") && R.isIgnored(".env")); })()
tests.fail: Create the repository inside ~/my-site (cd my-site, then git init), and commit .gitignore with the lines node_modules/ and .env.

tests.name: node_modules and .env are not in any commit (neither yours nor on the server)
tests.check: (() => { const R = sim.repo("~/my-site"); const S = sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/my-site.git"); if (!R || R.root !== "/home/student/my-site") return false; const bad = (c) => Object.keys(c.files).some((p) => p.startsWith("node_modules/") || p === ".env"); return R.log("main").length > 0 && !R.log("main").some(bad) && !S.log("main").some(bad); })()
tests.fail: .gitignore must be created BEFORE git add . - otherwise node_modules and .env get into the first commit.

tests.name: The first commit contains the website files index.html, css/style.css, js/main.js
tests.check: (() => { const R = sim.repo("~/my-site"); const S = sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/my-site.git"); if (!R || R.root !== "/home/student/my-site") return false; const log = R.log("main"); const root = log[log.length - 1]; return Boolean(root && root.parents.length === 0 && root.files["index.html"] && root.files["css/style.css"] && root.files["js/main.js"]); })()
tests.fail: Add all website files to the first commit: git add . (after creating .gitignore).

tests.name: The work on the contacts was done in the feature/contacts branch
tests.fail: Create the branch with git switch -c feature/contacts and commit contacts.html in it.

tests.name:
contacts.html with the text

Contacts

is in main and on the server
tests.check:
(() => { const R = sim.repo("~/my-site"); const S = sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/my-site.git"); if (!R || R.root !== "/home/student/my-site") return false; const c = R.commit("main"); return Boolean(c && c.files["contacts.html"] === "

Contacts

\n" && S.files("main")["contacts.html"] === "

Contacts

\n" && R.log("main").some((x) => x.subject === "Add contacts page")); })()
tests.fail: Merge the branch into main: git switch main, then git merge feature/contacts (or --no-ff).

tests.name: The feature/contacts branch is deleted
tests.check: (() => { const R = sim.repo("~/my-site"); const S = sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/my-site.git"); if (!R || R.root !== "/home/student/my-site") return false; return !R.branches().includes("feature/contacts") && !S.branches().includes("feature/contacts"); })()
tests.fail: After the merge, delete the branch: git branch -d feature/contacts.

tests.name: The global alias lg is set up and used
tests.fail: Run git config --global alias.lg "log --oneline --graph --all" (with quotes), then git lg.

tests.name: main on the server matches the local one, the upstream is origin/main
tests.check: (() => { const R = sim.repo("~/my-site"); const S = sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/my-site.git"); if (!R || R.root !== "/home/student/my-site") return false; return R.remotes().origin === "https://github.com/anna/my-site.git" && R.commit("main") !== null && S.tip("main") === R.commit("main").hash && R.upstream("main") === "origin/main"; })()
tests.fail: Connect the server (git remote add origin ...) and push the branch: git push -u origin main.

tests.name: The tag v1.0 is on the server and points to the last commit (HEAD)
tests.check: (() => { const R = sim.repo("~/my-site"); const S = sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/my-site.git"); if (!R || R.root !== "/home/student/my-site") return false; const t = S.s.tags["v1.0"]; const h = R.commit("HEAD"); return Boolean(t && h && t.hash === h.hash && t.hash === S.tip("main") && R.tag("v1.0") && R.tag("v1.0").hash === h.hash); })()
tests.fail: Create the tag at the end, when everything is merged: git tag -a v1.0 -m "...". Tags are not pushed automatically - git push --tags or git push origin v1.0.

tests.name: The tag v1.0 is annotated (has a message)
tests.check: (() => { const R = sim.repo("~/my-site"); const S = sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/my-site.git"); if (!R || R.root !== "/home/student/my-site") return false; const t = S.s.tags["v1.0"]; const l = R.tag("v1.0"); return Boolean(t && t.message && t.message.trim() && l && l.message && l.message.trim()); })()
tests.fail: A lightweight tag git tag v1.0 does not store an author or a message. You need git tag -a v1.0 -m "First release".

tests.name: You are on main, the working directory is clean
tests.check: (() => { const R = sim.repo("~/my-site"); const S = sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/my-site.git"); if (!R || R.root !== "/home/student/my-site") return false; return R.branch === "main" && R.state() === null && R.status().clean; })()
tests.fail: At the end git status must answer nothing to commit, working tree clean.

tests.name: Other website files: all files are on the server, no secrets, the tag v1.0 is on HEAD
tests.fail: The solution must work with any website: add files with git add ., not by their names.

tests.name: Other website files: the tag is annotated, no branch, the folder is clean
tests.check: (() => { const R = sim.repo("~/my-site"); const S = sim.remote("https://github.com/anna/my-site.git"); if (!R || R.root !== "/home/student/my-site") return false; if (R.branches().includes("feature/contacts") || !R.status().clean) return false; const t = S.s.tags["v1.0"]; const l = R.tag("v1.0"); return Boolean(t && t.message && t.message.trim() && l && l.message && l.message.trim()); })()
tests.fail: Do not rely on specific file names: .gitignore, git add ., a branch, merge, tag -a, push --tags.

tests.name: The script ran without internal errors
tests.fail: Check the quotes in the commands.

hints: The order matters: first .gitignore, then git add . - then node_modules/ and .env do not get into the commit. Check git status -s: they must not be there.
Branch: git switch -c feature/contacts, the file with echo, git add, git commit. Merge from main: git switch main, git merge feature/contacts.
A merged branch is deleted with git branch -d feature/contacts.
Put an alias value with spaces in quotes: git config --global alias.lg "log --oneline --graph --all".
Create the tag last, when everything is merged: git tag -a v1.0 -m "First release".
A normal git push does not send tags: git push --tags (or git push origin v1.0).

questions.question: Why does a project need tags?
options: To create a new branch for work
To mark an important commit forever, for example version v1.0
To hide files from Git
To merge two branches
questions.explanation: A tag is a permanent "label" on a commit. Unlike a branch, it does not move with new commits.

questions.question: Match the command with the action.
pairs: Create an annotated tag on HEAD
Delete a tag on your computer
Push one tag to the server
questions.explanation: Creating and deleting a tag work locally, a tag gets to the server only through push.

questions.question: How does an annotated tag differ from a lightweight one?
options: It stores the tag author (Tagger) and the date
It stores a message
It moves forward with new commits
It is created with git tag -a
questions.explanation: A lightweight tag is just a name for a commit. An annotated tag is a separate object with an author, a date and a message. No tag moves.

questions.question: You ran git tag -a v1.0 -m "First release" and git push. There is no tag on GitHub. Why?
options: The tag is damaged
git push does not send tags - you need git push --tags or git push origin v1.0
GitHub does not support annotated tags
You must delete the branch first
questions.explanation: Tags are pushed separately: git push --tags (all) or git push origin v1.0 (one).

questions.question: git show v1.0 starts with the lines tag v1.0, Tagger: Anna Karimova ..., First release. What does this mean?
options: v1.0 is a branch
v1.0 is a lightweight tag
v1.0 is an annotated tag with the message First release
The commit is called First release
questions.explanation: Only an annotated tag has the tag/Tagger/message block. Below it comes the commit the tag points to.

questions.question: The version was 1.4.2. Match the change with the new version by semantic versioning.
pairs: Fixed a typo on a page
Added a blog page, old things still work
Completely redid the website, old links do not work
questions.explanation: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH: PATCH - fixes, MINOR - new features without breaking anything, MAJOR - incompatible changes. The lower numbers are reset to zero.

questions.question: A log line: 75d1cf9 (HEAD -> main, tag: v1.0, origin/main) Merge branch 'feature/contacts'. What is the name of the tag? Enter only the name.
questions.explanation: In brackets Git shows the labels of the commit: tag: v1.0 is a tag, origin/main is the branch on the server.

questions.question: Complete the command so that git st runs git status: git config --global ______ status
questions.explanation: Aliases are stored in the settings alias.<name>. If the command has spaces, the value is put in quotes.

questions.question: What is a release on GitHub?
options: The same as the main branch
A version page based on a tag: a title, a description of the changes and files to download
The git release command
A copy of the repository owned by another user
questions.explanation: A release is created on the website (Releases → Draft a new release) on top of a tag. Git knows nothing about releases - it is a GitHub feature.

questions.question: What is needed for the website to open through GitHub Pages from the main branch?
options: index.html is in the root of the branch
In Settings → Pages the source Deploy from a branch, the branch main and the folder / (root) are selected
Create the tag v1.0
The changes are pushed to GitHub with git push
questions.explanation: Pages publishes what is on GitHub in the selected branch. Pages does not need a tag.

questions.question: The GitHub login is anna, the repository is my-site. At what address will the website open on GitHub Pages?
options: https://github.com/anna/my-site
https://anna.github.io/my-site/
https://my-site.github.io/anna/
https://pages.github.com/anna
questions.explanation: A project address on Pages: https://<login>.github.io/<repository>/. github.com/anna/my-site is the code page, not the website.

questions.question: You created the tag v1.0 on the wrong commit, but have not pushed it yet. What should you do?
options: Delete the repository
git tag -d v1.0, then create the tag again on the right commit
git reset --hard
Nothing: the tag will move to the new commit by itself
questions.explanation: A tag that is not pushed can be safely deleted and created again. It is better not to rewrite a pushed tag: others may have already downloaded it.
